newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos vetoes Philippine budget curb on poll funds.
newsitem.headline: Ramos vetoes Philippine budget curb on poll funds.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos signed the 1997 budget into law on Wednesday but vetoed a provision which sought to restrict the use of funds to underwrite any election or plebiscite.
The presidential palace said in a statement that Ramos used his veto powers because the provision impinged on the "fundamental prerogatives" of the Commission of Elections.
Opposition politicans have said the use of the veto suggests that the government may be considering a plebiscite to amend the constitution, possibly to extend Ramos's six-year term in office.
"The possibility of holding a plebiscite to amend the constitution is now very distinct," opposition Senator Ernesto Herrera said.
"There is now a source of funding for this activity," he told reporters.

Ramos is restricted under the constitution to a single term in office, which is scheduled to end in mid-1998. Some groups have launched a move to amend the constitution, saying that the economic reforms launched by the president are in danger of withering away if he leaves office.
Ramos has said he is not interested in a second term in office and denied he has links with those campaigning for a change in the constitution.
